key_insight: Laser post-treatment reduced wear rates by approximately 24% for detonation-sprayed and 39% for gas-flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings, while producing deposition-dependent mechanical changes.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to more wear-resistant coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel, but deposition method matters when stiffness is also a design requirement.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying and gas-flame spraying, then apply laser post-treatment.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Measure hardness and elastic modulus by instrumented indentation and evaluate dry sliding with ball-on-disk tests.
evidence_signal: After treatment, DS hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV; wear rates fell from 1.939 to 1.465 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for DS and from 2.419 to 1.476 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for GFS.
watch_item: GFS elastic modulus decreased from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa after treatment, so improved wear resistance should not be equated with uniformly improved mechanical properties.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
